title: test: reproduce C388883 encoded pin aliases
description: Reproduces a bug where HTML-encoded pin aliases from EasyEDA are incorrectly processed, leading to invalid pin labels in generated components.
body:
## Why

Importing JLCPCB part C388883 (Panasonic EVQP7C01P) exposes a pin-label conversion bug. The EasyEDA payload represents the duplicate switch terminals with HTML-encoded backticks: `1`` and `2``.

The converter currently carries those encoded values directly into the generated component as aliases:

```ts
pin3: ["1`", "1"]
pin4: ["2`", "2"]
```

Those strings do not satisfy the tscircuit pin-label rules. When the generated component is evaluated, core emits `source_property_ignored_warning` entries and excludes both aliases. This means a successful `tsci import` can produce a component containing labels that are rejected when the component is used.

## What this PR adds

- The raw EasyEDA fixture for C388883.
- A focused regression repro that verifies the encoded terminal numbers are present after parsing.
- Assertions showing that the encoded values propagate into the generated TypeScript.
- Assertions for the downstream invalid-pin-label warnings.

This is intentionally a repro-only PR. It does not prescribe whether the eventual converter fix should decode, normalize, or omit these alternate terminal labels; it provides a concrete fixture and failure boundary for evaluating that fix.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C388883-to-ts.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: fix: export all schematic sheets in image downloads
description: Fixes schematic downloads to include all sheets in multi-sheet projects instead of just the firstdefault sheet.
body:
## Motivation

Projects can contain multiple `schematic_sheet` elements, but schematic PNG and SVG downloads used `convertCircuitJsonToSchematicSvg`. That renderer intentionally selects one sheet, so multi-sheet projects downloaded only their first/default sheet—for example, the `host` sheet in `mohan-bee/hub`.

`circuit-to-svg` already provides `convertCircuitJsonToStackedSchematicSheetsSvg`, which renders every sheet in `sheet_index` order and preserves the existing behavior for projects with zero or one sheet.

## Changes

- use `convertCircuitJsonToStackedSchematicSheetsSvg` directly for schematic SVG downloads
- use the same stacked renderer before rasterizing schematic PNG downloads
- use the standard `image/svg+xml` MIME type for SVG downloads

## Result

Schematic PNG and SVG downloads now contain every sheet in one vertically stacked image. Single-sheet projects continue to render normally. PCB, assembly, pinout, and 3D downloads are unchanged.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`
- Biome formatting check on both changed files

body:
## Summary

- add numbered `AutoroutingPipelineSolver11_Simplification`, a cleanup-only pipeline for existing `SimpleRouteJson.traces`
- use the conventional `BasePipelineSolver` definition with explicit prepare, simplify, apply, and DRC-validation stages; the outer pipeline does not override `_step()`
- keep stage work incremental: one input trace, one wrapped solver step, one output trace, or one validation pass per `_step()`
- preserve variable-width traces exactly and include them as immutable collision geometry while simplifying constant-width traces
- opt Pipeline 11 into clearance checks that use the actual current/neighbor trace widths and a matching spatial-search margin, without changing established pipeline behavior
- preserve trace IDs, connection metadata, endpoints, terminal vias, and terminal PCB-port metadata without routing missing SRJ connections

## Why

The `simplify` autorouting phase needs a dedicated local pipeline for users who want to improve traces that are already routed. Reusing the normal autorouting pipeline would solve SRJ connections again instead of limiting the work to post-route cleanup.

The cleanup solvers currently use one `traceThickness` per high-density route. Sending a variable-width SRJ trace through that representation collapsed every segment to one arbitrary width and created DRC violations. Pipeline 11 now makes that capability boundary explicit: constant-width routes are simplified, while variable-width routes retain their exact copper geometry and still block unsafe shortcuts.

Companion props PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/723

## Real-board visual snapshot

The fixture was captured from the board and MCU autorouting events produced by [imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller#files) at [`tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller@b4560e5`](https://github.com/tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller/commit/b4560e5).

Pipeline 11 preserves all 148 traces and every input width set, including 30 exact variable-width routes. It reduces route points from **1,829 to 1,763** and vias from **150 to 73**, while exact relaxed DRC remains **0 → 0**.

![RP2040 motor controller before and after Pipeline 11 simplification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/feat/simplification-pipeline/tests/__snapshots__/pipeline11-simplification-rp2040-motor-controller-visual-rp2040-motor-controller-before-after.snap.svg)

body: ### Motivation Capture a general schematic auto-layout failure where components from adjacent partitions are packed closer than the configured partition gap, which causes their rendered annotations to collide. The input was captured directly from the exact LedBlinker TSX using @tscircuit/core 0.0.1803 and @tscircuit/matchpack 0.0.88. It preserves the complete generated Matchpack problem and does not add manual schematic positions or a proposed fix. ### Current behavior C1 belongs to a standalone partition while C3 belongs to the main U1 partition. After layout, their body-to-body vertical gap is about 0.105 even though partitionGap is 1.2. title: Reroute component-to-component traces around avoidable label-trace crossings
description: Reroutes component-to-component traces to avoid crossings with generated net-label connectors, ensuring cleaner routing and preserving valid label-to-label crossings.

## Root cause

Component-to-component traces are routed before generated net-label connectors are added to the pipeline. A later connector can therefore cross an already-routed component trace even when that component trace has an equally short clean corridor.

Crossings between two generated label connectors are valid and remain unchanged.

## Solution

- track generated connector IDs explicitly instead of matching trace ID strings
- retain provenance for traces produced by the original component-routing pass
- after connectors exist, inspect only crossings between a fixed generated connector and an eligible component trace
- reuse the existing `generatePerpendicularTraceDetours` routing primitive, extended with optional bounds so an attached label and its connector form one obstacle
- accept only candidates that are no longer than the original route, preserve the turn budget, and avoid components, text, foreign labels, coincident traces, and all foreign-trace intersections

The previous standalone 331-line candidate generator has been removed. The cleanup now uses a compact coordinator around the existing routing primitive.

## Result

- the wireless-mouse component trace takes the available collision-free corridor
- generated connectors never move
- label-to-label crossings remain allowed
- routes without an equally short safe alternative remain unchanged

title: Align same-net pin exits, endpoint buses, and shared rails
description: Aligns adjacent same-side pin exits onto neighboring pin rows, aligns degree-two buses between perpendicular endpointload traces, and preserves generated connector junctions while validating candidates against various criteria.
body:
## Summary

- align adjacent same-side pin exits onto a neighboring pin row when the reroute is shorter and clear
- align degree-two buses between perpendicular endpoint/load traces onto both load rails
- align nearby first rails that leave the same endpoint in the same direction when doing so removes a visible jog
- align eligible generated label-connector rails without moving their labels or host traces
- preserve generated connector junctions when their host trace is aligned
- pass connector provenance from the producing solver instead of parsing trace ID strings
- validate every candidate against components, other-net traces, labels, moved attached labels, endpoint integrity, and newly introduced crossings
- support all rotations and reversed trace/endpoint ordering
- update 28 snapshots where the generic rules produce visually reviewed alignment improvements

## Root causes

The original junction heuristics only accepted reroutes that shortened visible geometry or matched a specialized return-bus topology. They therefore kept nearby parallel rails joined by small jogs even when the topology allowed one continuous rail.

The shared-endpoint candidate is topology-based: both traces must share a pin, depart along the same axis and direction, expose compatible perpendicular rails whose intervals touch after alignment, and keep the branch rail internal so no endpoint moves. Specialized return/bus candidates continue to run first.

Adjacent-pin exit alignment is also topology-based: it derives the departure and stem axes from pin facing directions, finds an outward donor segment shared by the nearby pin rows, and reroutes only when the branch already leaves through that stem. It does not depend on a fixed point count or H/V turn sequence.

Generated net-orientation connectors need two additional cases. An eligible connector can remove its own offset rail when it attaches inside a host segment and the aligned rails meet end-to-end. When a real host trace moves, an attached connector endpoint is projected onto the moved host along its existing segment so the junction remains connected. Connectors attached at donor corners, connectors that would overlap donor rails, and candidates that collide with any component, trace, or label remain unchanged.

## Verification

title: fix: clear copper pours around oval plated holes
description: Fixes the omission of oval plated holes in copper pour calculations, ensuring proper clearance and thermal relief for designs using oval plated holes.
body:
## Why

Circuit JSON supports plated holes with `shape: "oval"`, which are commonly used for through-hole battery contacts and similar elongated terminals. The copper-pour adapter handled circular, pill, and rectangular plated-hole shapes, but it did not convert oval plated holes into solver input pads.

Because the pad was omitted before obstacle processing, the solver had no geometry to subtract from a different-net copper pour. Copper could therefore extend into the required clearance around the plated hole. In the ATTiny85 Arcade Keychain this affected the oval battery pads and prevented the normal exported-board short/clearance validation from being trusted without adding board-specific keepouts.

This behavior should be fixed in the shared solver rather than in individual boards so every design using oval plated holes receives the configured clearance and thermal-relief behavior automatically.

## What changed

- Add an `InputOvalPad` type that preserves the outer width, outer height, position, and rotation from Circuit JSON.
- Convert `pcb_plated_hole` elements with `shape: "oval"` into solver input pads.
- Approximate the rotated ellipse as a polygon and apply the configured pad margin with a rounded geometric offset.
- Include oval plated holes in thermal-relief clearance generation.
- Add a regression test that verifies conversion, rotation, and the resulting 0.2 mm copper-clearance extents.
- Add SVG snapshot coverage for a rotated oval plated hole with four thermal-relief spokes.

title: fix: serialize concurrent tsci add installations
description: Serializes concurrent tsci add invocations to prevent overlapping package-manager processes that can race on package.json, lockfiles, and native dependency installation.
body:
Concurrent `tsci add` invocations in the same project currently start overlapping package-manager processes. This can race on `package.json`, lockfiles, `node_modules`, and native dependency installation. This was encountered when an agent issued three add calls in parallel during circuit generation.

Serialize adds with a project-scoped `proper-lockfile` lock, covering registry configuration, installation, and KiCad setup. Resolve the project real path so symlinked working directories share the lock. Release it on failure and recover stale locks after interrupted processes. Run install subprocesses asynchronously so long installs continue refreshing the lock heartbeat; serialize KiCad setup within multi-package adds as well.

Validation:

- New subprocess regression fails on the base branch with overlapping installs (`EEXIST`) and passes with this change. Covers a 12-second install exceeding the stale threshold, symlinked working directories, failure release, and stale-lock recovery.

title: fix: report autorouting pipeline progress
description: Fixes the autorouting progress reporting for Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9, ensuring accurate progress updates during routing operations.
body:
Autorouter diagnostics report `progress=0%` even as routing advances through pathing and high-density routing. In [this adm6-breakout release](https://tscircuit.com/seveibar/adm6-breakout/releases/65f0a6dd-aa34-490b-8f26-526a3db9442c), the captured logs contain 59 zero-percent routing updates; the separate fanout solver reports 100%.

Core's `TscircuitAutorouter` forwards the top-level solver's `progress`. Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9 inherit `BaseSolver.progress = 0` but do not implement `computeProgress()`, so that value never changes. Pipeline 9 Networked inherits the same issue from Pipeline 9.

Implement `computeProgress()` directly on Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9. It combines completed pipeline steps with the active solver's progress. Pipeline 9 Networked receives the calculation through inheritance. Routing behavior is unchanged.

Steps have equal weight: this is a completion indicator, not a time estimate. A step without its own progress estimate advances the percentage when it finishes.

Validation:
- A focused test verifies nonzero progress for Pipeline 7, Pipeline 9, and Pipeline 9 Networked.
- Existing Pipeline 7 and Pipeline 9 Networked contract tests pass.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` pass.

After release, consumers must refresh `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` in the core/runtime bundle. Core's progress-event implementation does not need a code change; this PR does not update the deployed builder.

title: Fix Bug Report 94 trace overlap in force solver
description: Fixes trace overlap issue in the force solver related to Bug Report 94, ensuring no overlaps remain in the autorouting process.
body: ## Before ## After ## Summary - pin `high-density-repair01` to the fix in https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair01/pull/17 - run the Bug Report 94 regression explicitly through `AutoroutingPipelineSolver9_PreloadedTraceGraph` - require at most 5 DRC errors and assert that neither the original `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` overlap nor a transferred overlap involving `source_trace_108` remains - update the deterministic macOS and Linux Pipeline9 snapshots ## Where the issue was The overlap is visible at the `highDensityRepairSolver` phase because that phase consumes the immediately preceding `highDensityForceImproveSolver` output. The bad geometry was already present in that input; the repair stage did not create it. Inside the actual `HighDensityForceImproveSolver`, the first force pass created the `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` proper crossing. The existing guarded rerun removed that pair but moved the collision to `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_99`, leaving the total DRC count at 6. This is why a visually clear snapshot and a passing `<= 6` assertion did not prove the defect was fixed. The upstream solver now validates residual route-pair clearance, restores a small aligned corridor from the original topology, adjusts only a newly affected neighbor when required, and accepts the candidate only when protected pairs remain clear and the local violation count strictly decreases. ## Why a later phase is not the primary fix A focused run of the existing `highDensityRepairSolver` on only the offending node left the `source_trace_108` / `source_trace_138` centerline distance effectively at zero, so merely increasing repair samples does not address this interior crossing. Pipeline9's later joint/reference DRC repair remains useful as a safety net, but it runs after stitching and simplification and is not guaranteed to select this local collision region. Fixing the geometry in the actual force solver removes the defect before every downstream phase and benefits every pipeline that uses that solver. ## Validation - focused Bug Report 94 Pipeline9 test on macOS: 5 DRC errors, no overlap involving `source_trace_108`, 2,578,699 iterations, 84.6 s - Linux CI Bug Report 94 Pipeline9 shard: same DRC/no-overlap assertions passed and the Pipeline9 snapshot was accepted - autorouter CI: build, type-check, format, Vercel, and all 9 Bun test shards passed - upstream solver CI: format, test, and type-check passed ## Pipeline9 same-machine benchmark Command: `/benchmark-all --pipeline 9 --same-machine` - [`dataset01` (85 scenarios)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33567287294): 100% completion, 100% relaxed DRC pass, 0 DRC issues, 0 timeouts, and 0 outcome regressions on both main and PR - [`srj18` (16 scenarios)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/33567288855): completion, relaxed DRC pass, and timeouts unchanged; 0 improved and 0 regressed outcomes; aggregate DRC issues changed from 74 to 75, isolated to `sample004`

The centered case also requires consistent clearance handling when a winding path leaves its own source pad, corner-aware boundary vias, and joint selection of plane routes when a greedy choice blocks another drop. Enumerate singleton plane candidates once instead of repeatedly regenerating their prefixes. For length matching, revisit excessive detours against completed copper and allow a differential pair's outer lane to move aside before tuning its mate. Searches retain bounded attempts, and complete copper is revalidated before accepting a result.

title: fix: derive CAD component size from model bounds
description: Fixes incorrect CAD component size calculation by deriving dimensions from the models bounding box instead of PCB footprint dimensions, ensuring accurate rendering of components.
body:
## Summary

- derive `cad_component.size` from the CAD model's own bounding-box extents when model bounds are available
- validate that every derived dimension is finite and positive, while preserving the existing fallback for models without usable bounds
- update the C165948 regression assertion and 3D snapshot to show the connector at its correct scale

## Why this change is needed

This is the fix for the behavior reproduced in #539.

The Parts Engine uses `convertEasyEdaJsonToCircuitJson` directly, so the emitted `cad_component.size` is preserved. Before this change, that size was assembled from the PCB footprint width and height plus an EasyEDA SVG height value. Those measurements describe different coordinate spaces and do not represent the OBJ model's local bounds.

For C165948, the OBJ metadata reports local bounds of approximately **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**, while the converter emitted **8.750224 × 5.648262 × 7.899984 mm**. Because the renderer uses `model_object_fit: "contain_within_bounds"`, the undersized 5.648262 mm Y constraint forced a uniform scale of roughly 0.715. The USB-C body was therefore rendered too small, leaving its shell mounting pads outside the model.

The generated-TSX path did not expose the bug because its `cadModel` output omits `size`; the direct Circuit JSON path used by the Parts Engine did.

## Implementation

When explicit `cadModelBounds` or embedded `_objMetadata.bounds` are available, the converter now calculates each local model dimension as `max - min` and uses those values for `cad_component.size`. It only accepts dimensions that are finite and greater than zero. If valid model bounds are unavailable, the converter retains the previous footprint-based fallback to avoid changing behavior for metadata-free models.

For C165948, the emitted size is now **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**, preventing unintended scaling and aligning the rendered connector body with its footprint.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-soup-tests/c165948-cad-footprint-size-repro.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/convert-to-soup-tests` — 28 passed

title: test: reproduce C165948 CAD footprint size mismatch

body:
## Summary

- add a regression test for the direct EasyEDA-to-Circuit-JSON conversion of C165948
- record the incorrect emitted CAD size metadata
- add a 3D snapshot with a PCB beneath the part so the CAD-to-footprint mismatch is immediately visible

## Why this PR is needed

Using `<connector standard="usb_c" />` resolves C165948 through the Parts Engine. That flow calls `convertEasyEdaJsonToCircuitJson` directly and preserves the generated `cad_component.size`.

For C165948, the OBJ metadata describes bounds of approximately **8.94 × 7.90 × 4.101 mm**, but the converter emits a CAD target size of **8.750224 × 5.648262 × 7.899984 mm**. The target X/Y values come from the PCB component bounds and do not describe the OBJ in its local coordinate frame. With `model_object_fit: "contain_within_bounds"`, the 3D renderer uses the limiting Y ratio (`5.648262 / 7.90 ≈ 0.715`) and uniformly shrinks the entire USB-C model. The footprint remains at its correct size, leaving the shell mounting pads visibly outside the rendered body.

There is already a C165948 3D test in the repository, but it converts through generated TSX. That generated `cadModel` does not include the problematic `size`, so it cannot reproduce the Parts Engine behavior. This new test deliberately exercises the direct Circuit JSON path used in production.

This PR only adds the reproduction and expected failing-state snapshot. It does not change converter behavior; a follow-up fix can update the asserted dimensions and snapshot.

title: Add autorouted physical-via export regression coverage
description: Adds regression tests and fixtures for physical-via export without altering existing implementations or introducing new production code.
body:
## Regression-only PR — the fixes are already merged

The actual fixes landed in [#158](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/pull/158) (physical layer precedence) and [#159](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/pull/159) (drill deduplication). Both are already merged into `main`.

This PR now targets current `main` and adds **only** the automatically generated fixture, provenance, three regression tests and two snapshots. Its production source and package metadata are identical to `main`. It does not replace or reapply the merged implementations.

**Merge guidance:** only this regression PR remains to consider for Gerber, because both fixes have already landed. There is no pending Gerber fix to stack above it. Normally the order is repro first, fix second; the upstream merges happened before this restructuring.

No coordinates, trace paths, copper pours, widths, or board dependencies are patched. The existing PR URL was retained.

## Reproduction

The committed fixture is unmodified output from published `tscircuit@0.0.2462`: two resistor-to-inner1 GND connections generated by automatic fanout on a four-layer board. Both physical vias span top–bottom, but their routing transitions stop at inner1. No PCB paths, manual traces, or manually placed routing vias were used.

This small fixture reproduces the export defect seen on the **complete RP2350 development board**, not merely its MCU essentials subcircuit. It is not itself a complete replica of that board.

![Generated fixture, top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/fix/physical-via-drill-spans/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/physical-via-spans-top.snap.svg)
![Generated fixture, bottom through-via annuli](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/fix/physical-via-drill-spans/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/physical-via-spans-bottom.snap.svg)

## Verification

Same machine, same inputs, old unfixed baseline `8af19f5c2e51459c4293c808fc1859beb92c653c` versus current upstream implementation `fa0a968` plus this regression coverage. Rechecked at this PR's `187bb0b` head:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three automatic-via regressions | 0 pass / 3 fail | 3 pass / 0 fail |
| Full test suite, including new regressions | 80 pass / 3 fail on old baseline | 113 pass / 0 fail on current main plus these tests |
| Package build + declarations | — | Pass |
| Typecheck | — | Pass |
| Two-via generated fixture | Incorrect `Plated,1,2,PTH` | Correct `Plated,1,4,PTH` |
| Complete RP2350 trial 19 | Four plated drill spans; 197 plated operations | One top–bottom plated span; 196 plated operations |
| Trial 19 non-plated locating holes | 2 × 0.65 mm | Unchanged |

Regression coverage includes reversed layer ordering, physical blind/buried spans, missing legacy layer lists, duplicated standalone vias, route-defined drill dimensions, and route-only inputs.

The current improvements are provided by merged #158/#159, **not new production code in this PR**. Build and typecheck were rerun and pass. Fresh CI runs apply to `187bb0b`; the earlier full-green run was on the superseded `7f3cd51` head.

Native KiCad drill export independently agrees on trial 19's physical inventory: **148 via holes + 44 header holes + 4 USB shell slots**, all through-board, plus two NPTH locating holes.

These are export checks, **not a claim that the RP2350 is fabrication-ready**. That local working trial still has five native routing/clearance errors and one shorted-net group. The board remains on unmodified published dependencies; no manufacturing order or project upload was made.

title: fix: deduplicate via drill hits and reconcile trace fallbacks
description: Fixes duplicate drill operations in Gerber file exports by deduplicating via drill records based on exact coordinates and drill diameter, ensuring accurate representation of physical vias without unnecessary fallback drills.
body:
## Summary

- Deduplicate via drill records by exact X/Y coordinates, drill diameter, and normalized physical layer span.
- Index explicit vias by position and diameter, then omit trace-derived fallback drills when one existing physical barrel covers the route transition. This works regardless of record ordering or trace IDs, since multiple traces may share a via.
- Preserve different drill sizes, distinct explicit or route-only spans, stacked barrels, nearby coordinates, and unmatched route-only vias. Non-via holes and slots are unchanged.
- Add 16 focused regression cases asserting structured Excellon commands plus a direct output-assertion test for the public Gerber/Excellon file exporter. No custom parsers, SVG generation, or snapshot assertions are used in these tests.

## Before / after snapshots

These snapshots use the **same five-location synthetic fixture and renderer**, counting operations parsed from the actual Excellon files. A normal PCB image hides coincident duplicate drills; this diagnostic makes the emitted hit counts and their layer spans visible.

### Before — 9 operations for 5 physical via locations

Captured from unmodified main at `1d49436` (`v0.0.102`) before applying the fix. Repeated records, explicit-via/route overlap, and a spurious shorter drill produce four redundant operations.

![Before: nine drill operations, including duplicate hits and a spurious blind drill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/0479b7fd0b5d99b0723fc890ce54dac887979c35/tests/excellon-drill/assets/via-drill-deduplication-before.svg)

### After — 5 operations, one per physical via

The genuine L1–L2 blind via and L2–L3 buried route-only via remain. Only duplicate hits and the unnecessary shorter fallback drill disappear.

![After: five drill operations with genuine blind and buried vias preserved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/0479b7fd0b5d99b0723fc890ce54dac887979c35/tests/excellon-drill/__snapshots__/via-drill-deduplication.snap.svg)

These images are retained solely as PR illustrations, linked to the earlier commit that captured them. Snapshot assets and rendering code have been removed from the current diff. The tests now assert exported drill commands, diameters, physical spans, and the exact drill-operation sequences directly.

## Verification

- Regression cases reproduce duplicate hits and incorrect fallback drill spans on the unpatched exporter.
- `bun test`: **110 pass, 0 fail**, including 17 new cases.
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`: pass.
- `bun run build`: pass, including declarations.
- `bun run format:check`: exits successfully; existing oversized JSON fixture notice only.
- `git diff --check`: pass.

This is an export-only fix: no routing, coordinates, copper geometry, or dependency versions are changed.

title: fix: prefer physical layers over legacy via drill endpoints
description: Fixes incorrect drill file generation by prioritizing physical layer spans over deprecated routing endpoints during Gerber file export.
body: ## Summary - Determine plated drill spans from the physical `layers` list before consulting deprecated `from_layer` / `to_layer` fields. - Retain normalized legacy endpoints when physical layers are missing or empty, and the through-board default when no span metadata is present. - Add 12 focused regressions for Gerber-file export, 2/4/6/8-layer through-vias, unsorted physical layers, actual blind/buried spans, legacy compatibility, single-span filtering, and input immutability. - Add a visual regression that compares exported bottom copper with the actual through-board Excellon drill openings. ## Problem During Bluetooth pedometer fabrication export, a physical through-via could have `layers: ["top", "inner1", "inner2", "bottom"]` while its deprecated routing endpoints described only a top-to-inner1 transition. The exporter preferred those endpoints and incorrectly emitted `drill-L1-L2.drl` rather than `drill-L1-L4.drl` with `Plated,1,4,PTH` metadata. Physical layer bounds now determine the drilled barrel. This change is limited to span precedence; drill-hit deduplication and trace-route fallback behavior are unchanged. ## Before / after snapshots The same three-via fixture is rendered from actual exported bottom copper (gold) and through-board drill openings (dark). All three vias physically span L1–L4. The left and center vias have conflicting legacy routing endpoints; the rightmost via is an unchanged control. | Before: unpatched exporter | After: physical-layer precedence | | --- | --- | | | | | Incorrect L1–L2 and L2–L3 drills leave two bottom pads without through holes. | All three holes are in the single L1–L4 drill file. | The **before** image was generated with the exporter source restored to baseline `8af19f5`, not simulated. The **after** image is the checked-in expectation in the [snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/blob/5a86fbd145db7776d61ecb560376f393f810b03c/tests/gerber/generate-gerber-with-physical-via-layer-precedence.test.ts). title: Export EasyEDA OBJ-only models through STEP siblings
description: Fixes the omission of 3D models in KiCad exports for components that only have OBJ URLs by deriving and embedding corresponding STEP models from EasyEDA.
body:
Follow-up fix for the merged repro in #496.

## Problem

The `seveibar/smd-usb-c` connector supplies only an OBJ URL from tscircuit's EasyEDA model CDN. KiCad export previously retained its footprint and pads but silently omitted its 3D body.

## Fix

For OBJ URLs on `modelcdn.tscircuit.com`, derive the corresponding EasyEDA `.step` sibling and pass it through the existing model download and packaging flow. This supports current `/assets/<part>.obj` URLs and the legacy `/download?...&pn=<part>` form.

The fallback is restricted to the recognized tscircuit CDN. Arbitrary OBJ URLs remain unsupported, and explicit STEP or WRL URLs retain priority.

## Regression coverage

The repro uses a vendored copy of the actual USB-C component and verifies that the source has OBJ only. It now requires:

- one exported footprint and all 22 pad/hole entries;
- one packaged `C165948.step` model;
- the correct `${KIPRJMOD}` model reference and download URL;
- successful rendering of the actual model in KiCad.

The exact STEP asset is included as a compressed, checksum-verified offline fixture.

![KiCad render with USB-C model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-to-kicad/142ab58bae6913d1f748b8202d7faaaa41db84a0/tests/pcb/repros/__snapshots__/repro31-usb-c-kicad-3d-missing-model.snap.png)

## Validation

- Repro plus existing model and remote STEP tests: 3 passed, 25 assertions.
- URL-boundary regression: passed (8 cases covering modern/legacy CDN URLs, malformed/unrelated URLs, and explicit STEP precedence).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- KiCad CLI 10.0.5 loaded and rendered the STEP model.

title: fix(schematic): normalize wrapped arc sweeps
description: Fixes rendering of Altium schematic arcs to correctly handle angles crossing zero degrees, ensuring accurate representation of wrapped arcs.
body:
Motive: Render Altium schematic arcs correctly when their angles cross zero degrees.

Altium arcs use a positive counterclockwise sweep, but the SVG renderer treated angles such as 360° to 90° as a −270° sweep instead of 90°, causing magnetic-core inductors and other wrapped arcs to appear distorted. This PR normalizes the arc sweep using a reusable helper, preserves full circles, and updates the relevant tests and snapshots without component-specific hardcoding or hacks.

description: Populates display_superscript when a name is displayed on more than one source electrical network, ensuring disconnected GND nets in sibling subcircuits render as GND and GND, while connected copies share one suffix and unambiguous names have none.
body:
Populates `display_superscript` when a name is displayed on more than one source electrical network. Unused source-net declarations do not create display conflicts. For example, disconnected GND nets in sibling subcircuits render as GND¹ and GND². Connected copies share one suffix; unambiguous names have none.

Applies to both `schematic_net_label` and trace-associated `schematic_text`, including inline display labels that have no `source_net`. Connectivity follows source traces, shared ports, and both forms of internal component pin connections across subcircuits. Scoped connectivity keys and matching names alone do not join networks.

Runs in the dedicated `SchematicLabelNetsWithConflictingNames` render phase after schematic label/symbol rendering and before PCB phases. The top-level group assigns suffixes for the whole circuit, with initial and dirty-update handlers and declared async dependencies. Clears stale suffixes when networks join and uses source member IDs for deterministic numbering even when Circuit JSON is reordered. Source names, connectivity, and unrelated schematic text remain unchanged. Updates circuit-json to 0.0.484 and circuit-to-svg to 0.0.413, which contain the schema and rendering support.

The latter allows a trace-clean layer move with residual via-pad issues to reach the following repair phase, while retaining via-trace and via-pair guards. Without it, the expanded checks exposed a five-error regression on SRJ18 sample 12.

Add indexed/reference span agreement and full sample-12 regressions. Via generation is unchanged.

The shared dependency has 89 passing tests and green CI. All 13,995 committed JSON fixture vias already use both endpoints; none uses a `layers` override.

title: Expand via-span DRC checks without routing changes
description: Normalizes DRC checks for vias to include all layers in their span, ensuring accurate collision detection across multiple layers without altering input geometry.
body:
Vias declared with `from_layer`/`to_layer` were checked only on their two endpoint layers, so a four-layer `top → inner2` via could intersect copper on `inner1` without a DRC error. Normalize the endpoint API to its inclusive board-layer span and use an explicit `layers` array directly when supplied.

The indexed DRC engine and circuit-json conversion share that normalization. HD conversion also uses the actual board layer count instead of assuming two layers. Added tests cover intermediate-layer trace and pad collisions, equivalent endpoint/array geometry, reversed and same-layer spans, invalid endpoints, and four-layer HD conversion. The checks leave input geometry unchanged.

This is the DRC-only portion of #95. It contains no solver or routing changes, no repair-stage scoring changes, no manufacturing-policy flag, no `addThroughViaLayersToTraces`, and no snapshot updates. Fixing the via-producing solvers, including investigating power-trace expansion, remains separate.

Validation: 88 local tests pass. The intermediate trace and pad collision reproductions both fail against the unchanged main DRC engine (it reports no collision), then pass with this change.

title: Fix DRC to check vias across their physical layer spans
description: Fixes DRC to ensure that vias are validated across their physical layer spans, preventing routing errors that could short copper on intermediate layers.
body:
Vias were indexed only on `from_layer` and `to_layer`, so repair could accept routes that shorted copper on intermediate layers or on other layers occupied by a through via. On a four-layer pedometer, a top→inner1 transition could therefore pass DRC while contacting a bottom-layer signal.

Resolve physical via layers once in a shared helper and use it in both `AutoroutingDrcEngine` and the Circuit JSON reference converter. Through vias occupy the full stack by default. When blind/buried vias are enabled, use the inclusive transition span or a validated explicit physical span. The converter also uses the actual board layer count for HD route coordinates.

- Consuming autorouter build (ESM and declarations) passes; its full pedometer regression changes from six via/trace violations with the unpatched engine to zero with this fix.

Each contains mode-1 arc records for the curved polarized-capacitor plate. The test does not modify or crop the source schematic. It verifies those real binary records and records the current broken full-sheet SVG snapshot. ## Visual Comparison | altiumviewer.tscircuit.com | Reference (Altium 365) | | :---: | :---: | | | | ## Expected behavior The renderer should select each component's active display-mode primitives, producing curved lower plates for all ten polarized capacitors, matching Altium 365. title: fix(site): enable vertical scrolling on left control panel
description: Fixes the inability to scroll vertically on the left control panel when content exceeds the viewport height on smaller screens.
body:
## Problem
On desktop and smaller laptop screens, the left `.control-panel` section cannot be scrolled vertically when content extends past the viewport height (e.g., on smaller displays, when error notices are displayed, or when download actions appear). This happened because `overflow: hidden;` was shared between `.control-panel` and `.viewer-panel`, clipping all overflowing content.

## Solution
- Removed `overflow: hidden;` from the shared `.control-panel, .viewer-panel` rule.
- Added `overflow-y: auto;`, `overflow-x: hidden;`, and `overscroll-behavior: contain;` specifically to `.control-panel`.
- Kept `overflow: hidden;` on `.viewer-panel` to preserve proper clipping for the preview frame's rounded corners.

## Verification
- Verified production site build via `bun run build:site`.
- Verified TypeScript checks via `bun run typecheck`.
- Formatted with Biome (`bun run format`).
